description: HOLDOUT test architecture (not used during development). Manually curated STRIDE ground truth for a CI/CD build-and-deploy pipeline. Flows are well-secured; the real risk lives in pipeline-specific configuration: a runner that executes untrusted PR code on a shared host with account-wide secrets, unsigned/mutable artifacts (supply-chain tampering), unprotected branches, unmasked secrets in logs, and an unapproved production deployer with cluster-admin credentials. Hard threats require CI/CD security knowledge and configuration reasoning; the deterministic baseline (which ignores config) cannot find them. easy = exactly what the attribute-based deterministic baseline detects.

threats.description: The internet-exposed source repository can be targeted by attackers impersonating developers or using stolen tokens.
threats.mitigation: Enforce SSO/MFA and short-lived tokens for repository access.

threats.description: The repository holds sensitive source and could leak it through misconfiguration or compromised accounts.
threats.mitigation: Restrict repository visibility and access, and scan for committed secrets.

threats.description: With branch protection off and no required reviews, an attacker or careless actor can push malicious code straight into the main branch.
threats.mitigation: Enable branch protection and require independent code review before merge.

threats.description: The runner executes untrusted pull-request code on a shared host, so attacker-controlled build steps can run with the runner's privileges and reach other pipelines.
threats.mitigation: Run untrusted PR builds in isolated, ephemeral sandboxes with no standing privileges.

threats.description: The runner's secrets are scoped to all pipelines, so untrusted build code can exfiltrate credentials belonging to unrelated projects.
threats.mitigation: Scope secrets to the minimum pipeline and inject them only into trusted jobs.

threats.description: Without image signing or immutable tags, a build artifact can be replaced or overwritten, enabling a supply-chain attack on production.
threats.mitigation: Require signed artifacts (e.g. Sigstore) and immutable tags; verify signatures before deploy.

threats.description: The secrets store holds sensitive pipeline credentials that could be exposed if access is too broad.
threats.mitigation: Restrict access to secrets and rotate them regularly.

threats.description: Secrets are not masked in logs, so credentials can leak into build output and their exposure cannot be cleanly attributed or contained.
threats.mitigation: Mask secrets in logs and audit secret access.

threats.description: The deployer holds cluster-admin credentials and requires no deployment approval, so any triggered pipeline can push arbitrary changes to production.
threats.mitigation: Require deployment approval and scope deploy credentials to least privilege.

threats.description: Without approval gates or deploy records, production deployments cannot be reliably attributed to a responsible actor.
threats.mitigation: Require approvals and keep an immutable, signed deployment audit trail.
